about.title: Pittsburg Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You're walking through a Railroad Avenue storefront or across a Harbor Street parking lot in Pittsburg, and the ground simply isn't where you expected it—a slick patch, a lifted curb, a stairway missing its railing. Later, once the ankle swells or the wrist refuses to bear weight, the question becomes who was responsible. In Contra Costa County, as across California, that answer turns on notice: whether the owner knew about the hazard, or reasonably should have, and failed to fix it or warn you. That's why the first few days matter. Photograph the exact spot, write down the time, and request that any camera footage be preserved, because many businesses overwrite recordings within weeks. We handle premises liability claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You're never obligated to hire us after your initial consultation.

items.title: Notice is the whole case
items.desc: California asks whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We know how to look for inspection logs, prior complaints, and cleanup schedules that show how long a problem was ignored.

items.title: Deadlines aren't all the same
items.desc: Most California premises claims carry a two-year limit, but a fall on city, county, or state property means a much shorter government claim window. Getting started early keeps those options open.

items.title: Shared blame doesn't end your claim
items.desc: Under pure comparative fault, being partly at fault—say you were looking at your phone—reduces a recovery rather than eliminating it. We can push back when an owner tries to pin everything on you.

items.question: I fell on a Pittsburg city sidewalk. Is that different from falling in a store?
items.answer: Yes, in an important way. When the property belongs to a public entity such as the City of Pittsburg or Contra Costa County, California requires a formal government claim first, and that window is generally six months rather than two years. The notice requirement still applies, so photos of the defect and its surroundings matter just as much. We can help sort out who actually owns and maintains the stretch where you fell.

items.question: The store manager already has video. Do I really need to do anything?
items.answer: You do. Surveillance systems often record over footage in a matter of days or weeks, and a business has no reason to keep it unless someone asks in writing. A prompt preservation request from our team puts the owner on notice not to erase it. In the meantime, take your own photos and get names of anyone who saw the fall.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to us?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle premises liability cases on contingency. That means no attorney fee unless there's a recovery, and you decide whether to move forward after the first conversation.
